key_insight: On-policy distillation (OPD) succeeds only when the teacher and student share compatible "thinking patterns" and the teacher contributes genuinely new capabilities beyond the student; diagnosing and enforcing these conditions yields reliable OPD gains.
problem_solved: Clarifies why OPD sometimes fails unpredictably and provides actionable criteria and a practical recipe so practitioners can know when and how to apply OPD effectively.
method: Systematic empirical analysis of OPD training dynamics across teacher-student pairs and tasks to identify success/failure patterns.

Characterization of two governing conditions: (a) compatibility of internal reasoning/behavior patterns between teacher and student, and (b) teacher-provided capability novelty above the student's current skillset.
Practical recipe combining diagnostic metrics, selective teacher sampling and targeted on-policy supervision to ensure compatibility and capability injection during distillation.
impact: Enables ML practitioners to predict OPD outcomes, choose or adapt teachers strategically, and apply focused distillation that reliably improves student models while avoiding wasted compute and negative transfer.
visual_elements: Venn diagram showing overlap of teacher vs. student capabilities with a highlighted 'novelty' region required for OPD benefit
Flowchart of the recommended OPD recipe: diagnose compatibility -> select/modify teacher -> targeted on-policy sampling -> monitor metrics
Bar/line chart comparing student performance trajectories under successful vs. failed OPD conditions
Iconic checklist illustrating the two success conditions (compatible thinking patterns, capability novelty)
paper_title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
paper_authors: Yaxuan Li, Yuxin Zuo, Bingxiang He, Jinqian Zhang, Chaojun Xiao
